details:
**"Mr. Gorbachev, tear down this wall!"**
The most famous line of Reagan's 1987 speech at the Brandenburg Gate in West Berlin, delivered with West German chancellor Helmut Kohl present. Reagan also urged Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev to "open this gate," and the line is a near-universal giveaway for him.

**Attempted assassination by John Hinckley Jr.**
In March 1981, barely two months into Reagan's presidency, John Hinckley Jr. shot him outside the Washington Hilton hotel in an effort to impress actress Jodie Foster. Reagan joked to his wife Nancy, "Honey, I forgot to duck," Secret Service agent Jerry Parr pushed him into the limousine, and Secretary of State Alexander Haig wrongly claimed "I am in control here" at the White House.

**James Brady and the Brady Bill**
Reagan's press secretary James Brady was left permanently disabled by a gunshot wound to the head in the Hinckley shooting. The 1993 Brady Handgun Violence Prevention Act, signed by Bill Clinton, was named for him and created a federal background-check system for gun purchases (NICS). Part of the law was struck down in Printz v. United States (1997) as a violation of the Tenth Amendment.

**Iran-Contra affair**
A scandal in Reagan's second term in which administration officials secretly sold arms to Iran and used the profits to fund the Contra rebels fighting Nicaragua's Sandinista government. This violated the Boland Amendment, which banned such aid, and was investigated by the Tower Commission, which criticized Reagan's detached management style.

**"A Time for Choosing"**
Reagan's 1964 televised speech supporting Republican presidential candidate Barry Goldwater, also called the "Rendezvous with Destiny" speech. It ends by borrowing FDR's line "You and I have a rendezvous with destiny," raised large sums for Goldwater, and launched Reagan's political career.

**Challenger disaster speech**
Reagan's 1986 address after the space shuttle Challenger exploded shortly after launch, killing its seven crew members. Quoting the poem "High Flight," he said they had "slipped the surly bonds of earth to touch the face of God," and compared them to the explorer Francis Drake, who "lived by the sea, died by the sea, and was buried at sea."

**Governor of California and Berkeley**
Reagan defeated incumbent Pat Brown in 1966 to become governor of California after promising to "clean up the mess at Berkeley," and won reelection in 1970 over Jesse "Big Daddy" Unruh. In 1969 he sent the Highway Patrol and National Guard against the People's Park protests in Berkeley, where one bystander was killed. As governor he also signed the first no-fault divorce law in the US and a 1967 law liberalizing abortion that he later regretted.

**Mulford Act**
A 1967 California law signed by Governor Reagan that banned carrying loaded firearms in public. It was aimed at the armed patrols the Black Panther Party used to monitor police.

**Air traffic controllers' strike (PATCO)**
In 1981 Reagan fired more than 11,000 striking members of the Professional Air Traffic Controllers Organization (PATCO) who ignored his order to return to work. The move was a major blow to organized labor in the United States.

**Election of 1980 and "There you go again"**
Reagan defeated incumbent Jimmy Carter amid the Iran Hostage Crisis and a weak economy, with John B. Anderson running as an independent. In a debate he deflected Carter's attacks with "There you go again" and asked voters, "Are you better off than you were four years ago?" Iran released the American hostages minutes after Reagan was inaugurated.

**Reaganomics and "voodoo economics"**
Reagan's economic program of tax cuts, deregulation, and reduced domestic spending, based on supply-side economics. George H.W. Bush, his 1980 primary rival and later vice president and successor, derided it as "voodoo economics."

**Strategic Defense Initiative ("Star Wars")**
Reagan's 1983 proposal for a missile defense system, partly based in space, that would shoot down Soviet nuclear missiles. Critics nicknamed it "Star Wars," and it was a sticking point at the 1986 Reykjavik Summit with Gorbachev.

**Election of 1984 and "Morning in America"**
Reagan won reelection in a landslide over Walter Mondale, helped by the "It's morning again in America" ad celebrating the economic recovery. In a debate he joked that he would not "exploit, for political purposes, my opponent's youth and inexperience," defusing concerns about his own age.

**INF Treaty and the Reykjavik Summit**
Reagan and Gorbachev's 1986 summit in Reykjavik, Iceland, nearly reached a deal to eliminate nuclear weapons but collapsed over SDI. Their 1987 Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces (INF) Treaty eliminated an entire class of nuclear missiles.

**Invasion of Grenada (Operation Urgent Fury) and the bombing of Libya**
In 1983 Reagan ordered the invasion of Grenada after a coup in which Prime Minister Maurice Bishop was killed. In 1986 he ordered air strikes on Libya (Operation El Dorado Canyon) after a terrorist bombing of a West Berlin discotheque, following earlier clashes with Libya in the Gulf of Sidra.
